articles.author: ZEUS LAB
articles.description:
A 60% win rate, and the account can still lose half of itself on the way.
That is not a rare streak of bad luck. With a 60% win rate, an average win of 0.8 times the average loss, and 10% of the balance at stake on every trade, 36.860% of 5,000 simulated paths touched half of the starting balance at least once within 200 trades. The 10% is not arbitrary: it is the Kelly fraction for those inputs.
Every number below is a calculation from our free in-browser calculator, with the same formulas and the same random seed. It is not a forecast and not trading advice. The model is deliberately simple: every trade is independent, wins b units per unit risked with probability p and loses 1 unit with probability 1 − p, with p and b fixed. So a win multiplies the balance by (1 + b × stake) and a loss …
articles.title: A 60% win rate can still halve the account: risk of ruin and the Kelly fraction over 5,000 seeded paths

Project page: jarvisosorio.com/agent-session-scrubber

Source: github.com/JarvisOsorio/agent-session-scrubber

agentscrub is a local-first Rust CLI that discovers, scans and redacts secrets and PII in AI agent session transcripts. It runs offline, with no accounts and no telemetry.

scan — detect secrets and PII (exit 8 if the scan is incomplete)

How a 10-year physical business owner forced an AI to stop typing perfect garbage and start observing reality.

articles.author: anders lee
articles.description:
I maintain a browser extension that shows live captions (and translated captions) on top of any tab: a video, a livestream, a web meeting. Audio is captured in the browser, streamed over a WebSocket to a server, and recognised text comes back sentence by sentence.
Starting a session got all the attention. Stopping was one line: close the socket. That line was the reason a lot of first sessions ended with an empty screen. This post is about what "Stop" has to mean in a streaming pipeline, and the extra wrinkles a Manifest V3 extension adds.
A streaming recogniser sends two kinds of results:
partial results: fast guesses that keep changing, good for showing "the app is listening";
final results: settled text. Only finals are split into sentences, translated and saved.
Finals always lag behin…
articles.title: "Stop shouldn't mean close: ending a live-caption session in a Manifest V3 extension without losing the last sentence"

The report detailed what happened three weeks earlier when an emergency Linux kernel zero-day landed on their desks. Fly runs bare-metal physical servers across dozens of colocation facilities worldwide, hosting customer workloads as lightweight microVMs on top of standard Linux hosts. They could not paper over this bug with a rolling configuration reload or a managed-cloud toggle.
In a single afternoon, they had to patch and reboot every physical hypervisor in their global fleet.
For a platform whose promise is effortless global deployment—type fly deploy and your code spins up in Tokyo, Amsterdam, and Virginia in seconds—watching…
